title: Noether finiteness for a finite-type domain over a field
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field] and A an integral domain which is a finite-type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let K be a fraction field of A and L/K a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], with compatible A-algebra structures. Then the integral closure of A in L [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

proof.text: The attached declaration is already proved in the source library. Its proof first applies Noether normalization: choose an injective finite map from a polynomial ring P=k[X_1,...,X_n] into A. The fraction field K of A is then finite-dimensional over Frac(P), by localizing a finite P-spanning family of A. Transitivity makes L finite-dimensional over Frac(P) as well. All scalar structures are the compositions through A and K, so the required towers commute.

Apply the proved polynomial-ring case MvPolynomial.finite_integralClosure in that same source module to P and L. It gives a finite P-module N_P=integralClosure P L. (That source theorem handles inseparability by a finite coefficient-field and Frobenius root extension before applying the separable integral-closure finiteness theorem.)

Since A is finite, hence integral, over P, every element of N_A=integralClosure A L is integral over P by transitivity. The inclusion N_A into N_P is an injective P-linear map. The polynomial ring P is Noetherian, so this submodule of a finite P-module is finite. Its P-module generators also generate N_A over A; hence N_A is finite over A. This is exactly the conclusion of the attached source theorem, whose axiom check has no sorryAx.
